For users who don't need Photoshop's professional features but want Adobe quality design tools, Adobe Express provides a more accessible creative experience, particularly suitable for social media operations and content marketing teams.
clipchamp: Clipchamp is a free online video editor acquired by Microsoft and built into Windows 11, known for its extremely simple intuitive interface and rich built-in resources (templates, music, effects, stickers), an ideal tool for entry-level video creators. Provides multi-track timeline, filters, transitions, text animations, and picture-in-picture features for basic video editing needs. AI caption features automatically generate and sync subtitles, dramatically reducing caption production time. Built-in royalty-free music library and video stock library let creators work without copyright concerns. Directly integrates with OneDrive and Microsoft 365 with videos saved to the cloud. Offering a free tier (with watermark export limitations) and Clipchamp Premium paid tier (watermark-free and HD export), it is a convenient solution for Windows users to quickly create video content without installing third-party software.
pictory: Pictory is an AI-powered video content creation platform focused on automatically converting long-form text content (blog articles, scripts, meeting recordings) into short videos, dramatically lowering the barrier to video creation. Enter an article URL or text script, and AI automatically extracts key sentences, matches stock video footage, adds captions and background music, generating shareable video content within minutes. Particularly suitable for repurposing blog content into social media videos, YouTube Shorts, and marketing materials. Long video auto-editing extracts highlights, while portrait video caption features enhance the viewing experience. Offering 14-day free trials and multiple subscription tiers, it is an efficient tool for content marketing teams, podcasters, and bloggers to quickly convert existing content into video without video editing expertise.
invideo: InVideo is a full-featured online video creation platform offering 6,000+ professional templates, built-in media library (royalty-free video, images, and music), and AI assistance features to help marketers, content creators, and businesses quickly produce professional videos. AI Script Generator automatically creates video scripts based on topics, with AI voice synthesis supporting 50+ language dubbing to quickly convert text scripts into complete videos. Supports multi-person collaborative editing for teams to jointly create and manage video projects. The new InVideo AI version further simplifies workflows, generating videos from a single sentence description. Offering a limited free tier and Business and Unlimited paid subscription plans, used by over 8 million users globally, it is a popular tool for small businesses, social media teams, and digital marketers to rapidly produce video content.
openai: OpenAI is currently the world's most influential artificial intelligence research company, creator of epoch-defining products including ChatGPT, GPT-4, DALL-E, Whisper, and Sora. The OpenAI API platform lets developers call top language models like GPT-4o, o1, and o3, as well as DALL-E image generation models, to build AI-powered applications. The Assistants API provides persistent conversation and file analysis capabilities, while the Fine-tuning API supports custom model training. OpenAI Playground is an interactive tool for testing model capabilities. The open-source Whisper speech recognition model excels at multilingual transcription. OpenAI is led by Sam Altman with Microsoft as its primary investor, deeply collaborating on products like Copilot. Billed by token usage with some free trial credits, it is one of the most important infrastructure providers for building AI products.
huggingface: Hugging Face is the GitHub of the AI community and machine learning models, aggregating over 900,000 pre-trained models, 200,000 datasets, and 300,000 Spaces (runnable ML applications), the world's largest open-source AI model sharing platform. The Transformers library is the core tool for NLP and computer vision tasks, simplifying usage and fine-tuning of top models from BERT and GPT to Llama and Stable Diffusion. The Inference API supports one-line code deployment and model invocation. AutoTrain no-code training platform enables non-technical users to fine-tune models. The Hub hosts top open-source models including Meta Llama, Mistral, and Qwen, the preferred platform for downloading and publishing models. For AI researchers, ML engineers, and developers looking to leverage open-source models, Hugging Face is an indispensable core platform.
replicate: Replicate is a cloud platform for running open-source machine learning models through APIs, enabling developers to run tens of thousands of open-source models including Stable Diffusion, Llama, and Whisper within seconds without configuring GPU servers. Simple and intuitive to use, requiring just a few lines of Python or cURL code to call models and receive outputs. Supports deploying custom models (packaged with the Cog tool) as external API services. Charged by actual compute time with no upfront fees, suitable for projects with variable API call frequencies. The model marketplace aggregates large numbers of popular community-contributed models, from text-to-image to voice cloning. For developers who want to quickly integrate AI capabilities without managing infrastructure, Replicate is the most convenient solution for exposing open-source models as APIs, deeply popular with independent developers and startups.
langchain: LangChain is the most popular development framework for building LLM (Large Language Model) applications, providing core abstractions including Chains, Agents, Memory, and Tools to simplify complex AI application development workflows. Supports unified interfaces for all major LLM providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, Google, as well as vector databases like Pinecone and Weaviate. LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) supports declarative chain composition. LangSmith provides debugging, testing, and monitoring for AI applications. LangGraph supports building multi-agent workflows. Used by hundreds of thousands of developers globally to build RAG applications, AI assistants, data analysis agents, and various LLM applications. Completely free and open-source with over 90,000 GitHub Stars, it is the most influential framework in LLM application development.
llamaindex: LlamaIndex (formerly GPT Index) is a data framework focused on connecting private data to LLMs, with its core capability being building RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems that enable AI to answer precisely based on users' own knowledge bases. Supports importing and indexing from PDF, Word, web pages, databases, Notion, Confluence, and many other data sources, providing multiple retrieval strategies (vector retrieval, keyword retrieval, hybrid retrieval) to optimize answer quality. LlamaCloud provides managed data processing and retrieval services. Seamlessly integrates with LLM providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face. Workflows support building complex multi-step AI Agent processes. Completely free and open-source with millions of monthly npm/pip downloads, it is the preferred framework for building enterprise knowledge Q&A systems and document intelligence analysis applications.
pinecone: Pinecone is a fully managed vector database designed specifically for AI applications, specialized in storing and retrieving high-dimensional vector embeddings with support for ultra-low latency semantic similarity search, the core infrastructure for building RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems and semantic search applications. Seamlessly integrates with Embedding models from OpenAI, Cohere, and Hugging Face, efficiently indexing text, images, and other content after conversion to vectors. Supports metadata filtering and hybrid search (vectors + keywords) for complex retrieval scenarios. Fully managed Serverless architecture requires no operations with automatic scaling based on storage and query volume. Offering a permanent free tier (1GB storage) and paid production plans, used by many well-known enterprises including Notion and HubSpot for AI features, it is the product with the largest market share in the vector database space.
weaviate: Weaviate is an open-source vector database known for its native support for multi-modal (text, image, video, audio) vector storage and powerful modular AI integration capabilities. Built-in direct integration with Embedding models from OpenAI, Cohere, and Google automatically vectorizes data during import, eliminating separate Embedding steps. GraphQL API provides a flexible query interface, while hybrid search (BM25 + vectors) enables precise semantic retrieval. Weaviate Cloud Service provides a fully managed cloud version. Supports self-hosted deployment for complete data sovereignty. Completely free and open-source (BSD license) with an active open-source community, it is the most powerful open-source alternative to Pinecone, widely popular in enterprises valuing data sovereignty and wanting to reduce cloud service costs.
chroma: Chroma is a lightweight open-source vector database designed specifically for AI developers, known for its minimal API and excellent local development experience, the simplest choice for rapidly prototyping RAG applications and AI assistants. Supports local in-memory, local persistent, and client/server deployment modes for seamless migration from Notebook prototyping to production services. Python and JavaScript SDKs are intuitively designed, with just a few lines of code to complete vector storage and similarity retrieval. Deeply integrated with LangChain and LlamaIndex, it is one of the default recommended vector databases for both major LLM frameworks. Completely free and open-source (Apache 2.0 license) with over 15,000 GitHub Stars, used by large numbers of developers globally for learning vector databases, rapid prototyping, and small-to-medium scale production deployments, making it the most beginner-friendly choice in the vector database space.
python: Python is one of the world's most popular programming languages, consistently ranking at the top of the TIOBE index and Stack Overflow surveys for multiple years. Known for its clean and readable syntax, rich standard library, and massive third-party ecosystem (pip package management with over 500,000 packages). It holds an absolute dominant position in data science and AI, with core libraries like NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and scikit-learn building a complete ML/AI development ecosystem. The web development space features mature frameworks like Django and Flask/FastAPI. Automation scripts, system operations, and DevOps toolchains also make heavy use of Python. The official Python website provides interpreter downloads, documentation, and tutorials, making it the best introductory language for learning programming and pursuing data science. Completely free and open-source, maintained by the Python Software Foundation, it is one of the essential programming languages for every technical professional.
nodejs: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime environment based on Chrome's V8 engine, enabling JavaScript to run server-side and becoming the foundation of full-stack JavaScript development. Its event-driven, non-blocking I/O model excels at handling high-concurrency I/O-intensive tasks (such as API servers and real-time applications). npm (the world's largest software package registry) is installed with Node.js, providing over 2 million open-source packages. Frameworks including Express.js, Fastify, and NestJS build a rich web service development ecosystem. Electron uses Node.js to build cross-platform desktop applications. Used by top companies including Netflix, LinkedIn, and Uber for high-performance backend services. Completely free and open-source, maintained by the OpenJS Foundation, it is an indispensable foundational component in modern web development stacks.
golang: Go (Golang) is a statically typed compiled language released by Google in 2009, known for clean syntax, fast compilation speed, excellent concurrency performance (goroutines and channels), and low memory footprint. Compiles to a single executable file making deployment extremely simple with no runtime dependencies. Built-in concurrency primitives make writing high-performance microservices and network tools natural and intuitive. Cloud-native infrastructure tools including Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and Prometheus are all written in Go, making Go the preferred language for DevOps and cloud-native tool development. Rich standard library allows completing many tasks without extensive third-party dependencies. Completely free and open-source, primarily developed by Google, it is an important language with continuously rising influence in backend development and cloud-native tool development.
rust: Rust is a systems-level programming language developed by Mozilla and now maintained by the Rust Foundation, known for memory safety (memory management without garbage collection), ultimate performance, and zero-cost abstractions, winning the Stack Overflow Most Loved Programming Language title for 9 consecutive years. Ownership and the Borrow Checker eliminate memory safety vulnerabilities at compile time, serving as a safe alternative to C/C++. Adopted by Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta in safety-critical systems; the Linux kernel has incorporated Rust code, and Rust holds an important position in the WebAssembly ecosystem. The learning curve is steep, but mastering it enables writing high-performance, memory-safe systems software. The Cargo package management tool offers an excellent experience with the crates.io ecosystem continuously expanding, making it an important language for systems programming and WebAssembly development.
java: Java is Oracle's object-oriented programming language that has been the mainstream choice for enterprise-grade backend development since its 1995 release, with the JVM's write once, run anywhere characteristic making cross-platform deployment extremely convenient. The Spring Boot framework is the industry standard for building Java microservices and REST APIs, while Maven and Gradle manage complex dependencies. Android applications have long used Java as the primary development language (now gradually replaced by Kotlin). In core systems of large enterprises in finance, telecommunications, and government, Java remains the dominant technology stack. The JVM ecosystem (Kotlin, Scala, Groovy) shares Java's rich library resources. Both Oracle JDK and OpenJDK provide free versions, making it an important foundational language for enterprise backend development and Android development.
kotlin: Kotlin is a modern statically typed programming language developed by JetBrains, 100% interoperable with Java, with more concise syntax, and Null Safety features that eliminate common null pointer exceptions at the language level. Announced by Google as the official Android development language in 2017, it has become the preferred language for Android app development with over 95% of Android Top 1000 apps containing Kotlin code. Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) supports sharing business logic code across Android, iOS, Web, and desktop platforms, an important new direction for cross-platform development. The Spring framework provides first-class Kotlin support with an increasingly mature server-side Kotlin development ecosystem. Ktor is JetBrains' Kotlin-native web framework. Completely free and open-source, it is the core language every Android developer must master.
swift: Swift is a modern programming language for Apple platforms (iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS) released by Apple in 2014, known for safety (optional types), concise syntax, and excellent performance, having completely replaced Objective-C as the preferred language for Apple development. The SwiftUI declarative UI framework makes iOS and macOS interface development more concise and efficient. Swift Playgrounds supports interactive Swift learning. Swift Concurrency (async/await) elegantly handles asynchronous operations. Swift Package Manager manages dependencies. Server-side Swift (Vapor framework) extends Swift into backend development scenarios. Completely free and open-source (swift.org) with an active open-source community on GitHub. An essential skill for every Apple platform developer and the most important programming language in the Apple ecosystem.
typescript: TypeScript is a JavaScript superset developed by Microsoft, making the development, refactoring, and maintenance of large JavaScript projects safer and more reliable through a static type system. Compiles to standard JavaScript, compatible with all JS environments. Features like type inference, interfaces, generics, and enums dramatically improve code readability and IDE intelligent hints. Virtually all mainstream frontend frameworks (React, Vue, Angular, Next.js, etc.) provide first-class TypeScript support. Both Deno and Node.js support running TypeScript files directly. Annual Stack Overflow surveys show TypeScript consistently ranking as one of the most loved languages. Completely free and open-source with over 50 million monthly npm downloads, it has become the standard configuration for modern web development and an essential tool for large team collaboration and maintaining complex codebases.
php: PHP is one of the world's most widely used server-side scripting languages, powering over 75% of websites on the internet (including WordPress, Facebook, and Wikipedia). With major updates in PHP 8.x versions, JIT compilation brings significant performance improvements, while modern language features like Named Arguments and Fibers breathe new life into PHP. Laravel is currently the most popular PHP framework, known for elegant syntax and a complete feature ecosystem; Symfony is the preferred enterprise-grade PHP framework. Composer package management and the Packagist repository provide rich third-party libraries. Hosting costs are low with virtually all shared hosting supporting PHP and extremely abundant learning resources. For web development beginners and WordPress ecosystem developers, PHP remains an important gateway into server-side development.
ruby: Ruby is an object-oriented scripting language designed by Yukihiro Matsumoto (Matz) with programmer happiness as its design philosophy, featuring extremely elegant and expressive syntax. The Ruby on Rails (Rails) framework is the pioneering framework for rapid web application development, with well-known products including GitHub, Shopify, Airbnb, and Basecamp originally built with Rails, whose Convention over Configuration philosophy influenced the entire web framework design philosophy. RubyGems and Bundler provide a mature package management ecosystem. Capistrano handles automated deployment while Sidekiq processes background jobs. Although smaller in market share than Python and JavaScript, it still has a loyal user base in teams prioritizing developer experience and rapid prototyping. Completely free and open-source, with companies like Shopify continuing to contribute to the Ruby and Rails ecosystems.
react: React is the JavaScript user interface library open-sourced by Meta (Facebook), fundamentally transforming frontend development paradigms with its declarative programming model and component-based architecture, now the world's most popular frontend framework with over 20 million weekly npm downloads. The virtual DOM mechanism optimizes rendering performance, while Hooks (useState, useEffect, etc.) give function components complete state management capabilities. The vast ecosystem includes React Router (routing), Redux/Zustand (state management), and React Query (data fetching). Next.js and Remix build full-stack capabilities on top of React. React Native uses the same component model for cross-platform native app development. Completely free and open-source, heavily used by Meta, Airbnb, Twitter, Netflix, and other top companies, mastering React is an essential core skill for frontend developers and an important threshold for entering modern web development.
vue: Vue.js is a progressive JavaScript framework created by Evan You, known for its friendly learning curve, flexible integration approach, and excellent developer experience, with extremely high adoption in Chinese internet companies and Asian markets. Vue 3 was rewritten with the Composition API and TypeScript, with significantly improved performance and similar but more intuitive approach compared to React Hooks. Single File Components (.vue files) encapsulate templates, scripts, and styles in one file for an extremely smooth development experience. Nuxt.js provides a full-stack framework based on Vue, while Pinia is the officially recommended state management solution. Completely free and open-source, community sponsorship-driven, with Vite's official support pushing Vue development experience to its peak. It is the mainstream frontend technology choice at Chinese internet giants like Alibaba, Tencent, and Bilibili, and one of the world's most popular frontend frameworks.
angular: Angular is an enterprise-grade TypeScript frontend framework maintained by Google, known for its complete MVC architecture, strong typing, dependency injection, and built-in toolchain, suitable for long-term maintenance and team collaboration in large enterprise applications. Provides built-in features including routing, HTTP client, form management, and testing tools out of the box, reducing technology selection decision costs. Angular CLI provides scaffolding, build, test, and code generation tools. Zone.js provides automatic change detection, while RxJS reactive programming handles async operations. Widely used in large enterprises in finance, government, and insurance where code standards and maintainability requirements are high. Completely free and open-source, heavily used by Google, Microsoft, IBM, and other large enterprises. Although the learning curve is steep, its mature and stable ecosystem and strong type system maintain an important position in enterprise application development.
nextjs: Next.js is Vercel's full-stack web framework based on React, known for server-side rendering (SSR), static generation (SSG), API routes, and excellent performance optimization, having become the de facto standard for modern full-stack React development. The App Router introduced React Server Components, supporting server-side component rendering with streaming to clients for dramatically improved first-load performance. Built-in image optimization, font optimization, and code splitting achieve best-in-class web performance with zero configuration. Edge Runtime supports running in Cloudflare Workers and other edge environments. Completely free and open-source with over 8 million monthly npm downloads. The Vercel platform works perfectly with Next.js, making it the preferred framework for building modern web applications and full-stack projects, deeply beloved by developers globally.
nuxt: Nuxt is a full-stack framework based on Vue.js, providing SSR, SSG, file system routing, and auto-imports similar to Next.js, the best choice for Vue developers building production-grade applications. Nuxt 3 is built on the Nitro server engine, deployable to Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Workers, and other platforms. The Nuxt Modules ecosystem is extremely rich, with one-line configuration integrating Tailwind CSS, PWA, i18n, image optimization, and other features. Auto Imports automatically imports composables and components, reducing boilerplate code. The Nuxt Content module turns the file system into a content management system, suitable for blogs and documentation sites. Completely free and open-source, the most important full-stack framework in the Vue ecosystem, widely popular in Vue developer communities in Europe and Asia.
svelte: Svelte is an innovative frontend framework created by Rich Harris, taking a radically different compilation-time approach from React/Vue — compiling components into native DOM operation code with no runtime framework overhead, extremely small bundle sizes, and outstanding performance. No virtual DOM means component state changes map directly to DOM updates, requiring less and more intuitive code. SvelteKit is the full-stack framework based on Svelte with SSR, SSG, and file system routing. Has been voted Most Loved Framework in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey for multiple consecutive years. Completely free and open-source, particularly suitable for projects with extreme performance and bundle size requirements, and developers who want to experience a different mental model from React. Svelte's concise syntax and excellent developer experience are attracting an ever-growing number of developers to make the switch.
astro: Astro is a modern static site framework designed for content-heavy websites, known for its zero JavaScript by default philosophy, achieving component-level on-demand hydration through the Islands Architecture to dramatically reduce the JavaScript shipped to clients with extremely fast page loading. Supports mixing components from React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and other frameworks in the same project, with extreme framework neutrality. Built-in Markdown/MDX support makes it particularly suitable for building blogs, documentation, and marketing websites. Astro DB and Astro Actions continue expanding full-stack capabilities. Completely free and open-source, with glowing community reviews and rapid growth in 2023-2024, adopted by many tech blogs and documentation websites. It is the ideal site-building framework for developers and content creators pursuing ultimate page performance.
remix: Remix is a full-stack web framework created by React Router authors and acquired by Shopify, known for closely embracing web standards (Form, fetch, HTTP) and excellent data loading patterns. The nested routing system supports parallel data loading, with each route independently defining Loaders and Actions for elegant page data loading and form submission handling. Error boundaries and optimistic UI updates are built-in, with Progressive Enhancement ensuring basic functionality even without JavaScript. Built on React with deep Vite integration, deployable to multiple platforms. Completely free and open-source, with growing influence among developers pursuing web platform nativity and performance, it is one of Next.js's most notable alternative frameworks, particularly outstanding in data-intensive and content management application scenarios.
vite: Vite is a next-generation frontend build tool created by Vue.js author Evan You, completely solving the slow startup problem of traditional Webpack in large projects with extremely fast cold startup speeds (using native browser ES Modules) and lightning-fast Hot Module Replacement (HMR). Development environments require no bundling, directly using browser ES Module parsing — projects start in milliseconds regardless of size. Production builds are based on Rollup, outputting highly optimized static assets. Plugin API is Rollup-compatible with a rich ecosystem. React, Vue, Svelte, Lit, and other mainstream frameworks all officially support Vite. Completely free and open-source with over 10 million monthly npm downloads, it has become the core component of modern frontend toolchains, replacing Create React App as the preferred build tool for new projects.
webpack: Webpack is the foundational tool in the frontend build tool space, treating JavaScript, CSS, images, and other resources as modules, building a highly flexible asset processing pipeline through its Loader and Plugin systems. Modern frontend build concepts including code splitting, lazy loading, Tree Shaking, and Hot Module Replacement were all popularized by Webpack. Although gradually being replaced by Vite for new projects, Webpack 5's performance has improved significantly and it remains widely used in existing projects and enterprise applications. Popular toolchains including Create React App and Next.js (internal default historically) were built on Webpack. Completely free and open-source with a rich plugin ecosystem (over 10,000 npm packages) meeting various complex build requirements. For projects requiring highly customized build configurations, Webpack remains one of the most powerful options available.
github-actions: GitHub Actions is GitHub's built-in CI/CD and workflow automation platform, enabling developers to define automated pipelines directly in code repositories without integrating third-party CI tools. YAML-format Workflow files define trigger conditions (Push, PR, scheduled, etc.) and execution steps, supporting Linux, macOS, and Windows runtime environments. The Marketplace provides over 15,000 reusable Actions covering build, test, deploy, security scanning, and other scenarios. Matrix builds support parallel testing across multiple environments and versions simultaneously. Zero-friction integration with GitHub repositories, free for public repositories with per-minute billing for private repositories with free quotas. It has become the standard CI/CD tool for open-source projects, with testing and release workflows of many popular open-source projects relying on GitHub Actions.
jenkins: Jenkins is the oldest and most widely deployed open-source CI/CD automation server, supporting integration with virtually all build, test, and deployment tools through 1,800+ plugins. Pipeline as Code (Jenkinsfile) defines build processes as code, supporting both declarative and scripted syntax. Highly flexible extensibility enables support for scenarios ranging from simple builds to complex multi-stage release pipelines. Has a massive installed base in enterprise environments, particularly in Java and traditional enterprise application domains. Completely free and open-source but requires self-managed servers with relatively high operations costs. Although less user-friendly and modern than newer tools like GitHub Actions and CircleCI, its powerful customization capabilities and mature enterprise support keep it widely used in large enterprises.
circleci: CircleCI is a cloud-native CI/CD platform known for speed and developer experience, featuring extremely fast build speeds and intelligent caching strategies that dramatically shorten testing and deployment cycles. YAML configuration files are concise and intuitive, with powerful parallel builds and Orb reusable configuration components improving pipeline efficiency. Docker Layer Caching and dependency caching features significantly reduce repetitive build times. Deep integration with GitHub, Bitbucket, and GitLab supports one-click configuration. The Insights dashboard tracks pipeline performance to help continuously optimize CI/CD efficiency. Offering a free tier (6,000 build minutes/month) and usage-based paid plans, widely used at fast-growing startups and SaaS companies, it is a popular choice for teams pursuing ultimate CI/CD efficiency.
gitlab-ci: GitLab CI/CD is continuous integration and continuous deployment functionality built directly into the GitLab platform, completely integrated with code repositories, Issue tracking, and Merge Requests, enabling complete DevOps pipelines without configuring third-party tools. The .gitlab-ci.yml file defines pipeline stages and jobs, supporting parallel execution, conditional branching, and matrix builds. Auto DevOps automatically detects project types and configures default pipelines, enabling CI/CD with zero configuration. GitLab Runner supports execution on self-hosted servers, Kubernetes, or Docker environments. For teams hosting code on GitLab, built-in CI/CD is the most natural choice, avoiding the complexity of multi-tool integration and particularly popular in enterprises valuing data sovereignty.
terraform: Terraform is HashiCorp's Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool that defines and manages cloud infrastructure through HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language) declarative syntax, supporting over 3,000 providers including AWS, Azure, GCP, and Alibaba Cloud. The Plan command previews changes, Apply executes them, and State files track infrastructure state, forming a safe and controlled change workflow. The Module system supports reuse and encapsulation of infrastructure configurations. Terraform Cloud provides team collaboration and remote state management features. Used by hundreds of thousands of engineers worldwide to manage cloud infrastructure, it is one of the core skills for DevOps engineers and SREs. Offering open-source versions and Terraform Cloud paid tiers, it is the industry standard tool for implementing infrastructure version management and automated operations.
ansible: Ansible is Red Hat's most popular open-source automation tool, known for its agent-free, SSH-based simple architecture that defines server configuration, application deployment, and workflow automation tasks through YAML-format Playbooks. No Agent installation is required on target servers — managing thousands of servers through standard SSH connections reduces operational complexity. The massive Ansible Galaxy community provides thousands of ready-made Roles and Collections. Used together with Terraform to achieve a complete automation chain from infrastructure provisioning to application configuration. Ansible Tower/AWX provides a visual interface and role-based access control. Widely used in traditional IT operations automation and DevOps transformation scenarios, it is an important skill for system administrators and DevOps engineers.
kubernetes: Kubernetes (K8s) is Google's open-source container orchestration system that has become the industry standard for cloud-native application deployment and management, used by over 90% of Fortune 500 companies globally. Automates container deployment, scaling, load balancing, service discovery, and fault recovery to enable reliable application operation in large-scale distributed environments. The Helm package manager and rich ecosystem (Istio, Prometheus, ArgoCD, etc.) build a complete cloud-native toolchain. Managed Kubernetes services like GKE, EKS, and AKS lower the operations barrier. Under CNCF (Cloud Native Computing Foundation) governance with continuous development and frequent version updates. Although the learning curve is steep, mastering Kubernetes has become an essential skill for large internet companies and cloud-native architectures, making it the core infrastructure component of the containerization era.
helm: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes, known as the apt/yum for Kubernetes, simplifying the deployment, version management, and upgrade/rollback of complex applications on Kubernetes through Charts (packages containing Kubernetes resource templates). Helm Charts package complex multi-component applications (such as complete apps with Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, and Ingress) into single deployable units with parameterized configuration through values.yaml. Artifact Hub is the official Chart repository aggregating production-grade deployment templates for mainstream applications like Nginx, PostgreSQL, Redis, and WordPress. Helm 3 removed the Tiller component, dramatically improving security. Completely free and open-source, it is the standard tool for Kubernetes application deployment and management, greatly reducing the operational complexity of complex distributed applications.
prometheus: Prometheus is a CNCF graduated open-source system monitoring and alerting toolkit, renowned for its powerful multi-dimensional data model and flexible PromQL query language, becoming the de facto standard in cloud-native monitoring. Uses an active pull model for metric collection, gathering metrics from various systems and applications through Exporters. A powerful alerting rule engine combined with Alertmanager enables flexible alert routing and silence management. Deep integration with Grafana provides rich visualization dashboards, naturally complementing Kubernetes for container cluster monitoring. Thousands of official and community-maintained Exporters cover virtually all mainstream system components. Completely free and open-source, it is the core monitoring component in the Kubernetes ecosystem, deployed by large numbers of internet companies and cloud-native teams globally.
nginx: Nginx is the world's most widely used high-performance web server and reverse proxy server, known for its event-driven asynchronous architecture that efficiently handles tens of thousands of concurrent connections with extremely low memory footprint. Can serve as a static file server, a reverse proxy for dynamic applications (Node.js, Python, PHP), and can implement load balancing, SSL termination, HTTP/2 support, and access control. Nginx Ingress Controller is the most popular Ingress solution in Kubernetes. The nginx.conf configuration language is concise and powerful, supporting complex routing rules and traffic management. Over 35% of websites globally use Nginx including top platforms like Dropbox, Netflix, and WordPress.com. Completely free and open-source, with Nginx Plus commercial edition offering additional advanced features and technical support, it is a core infrastructure component of modern web architecture.
aws: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's largest cloud computing platform by market share, holding approximately 33% of the global cloud market and providing over 200 cloud services to millions of enterprises worldwide. Core services including EC2 elastic computing, S3 object storage, RDS databases, Lambda serverless functions, and CloudFront CDN form the infrastructure backbone of the modern internet. Well-known institutions including Netflix, Airbnb, and NASA are major AWS customers. AWS certifications are among the most valuable technical certifications in cloud computing. Offering a free tier for beginners to try, with production environments billed by actual usage. The vast service ecosystem and 33 global data center regions make AWS the preferred cloud platform for large enterprise digital transformation and startups building their technology stack.
azure: Microsoft Azure is Microsoft's enterprise-grade cloud computing platform and the world's second-largest cloud by market share, known for deep integration with Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory, SQL Server, and Microsoft 365, making it the natural choice for enterprise IT cloud migration. Provides a complete cloud service suite including virtual machines, Kubernetes, databases, AI services, DevOps tools, and hybrid cloud solutions. Azure AI services (including OpenAI service) are an important platform for enterprises deploying AI applications. Microsoft enterprise software license customers can enjoy significant cost benefits through Azure Hybrid Benefit. Leading market share in industries highly dependent on the Microsoft ecosystem including finance, government, and healthcare, Azure Active Directory (now Entra ID) is the world's largest enterprise identity management platform.
gcp: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is Google's cloud computing platform, excelling in big data analytics, machine learning, and container technology, ranking third in global cloud market share. BigQuery is the industry's most powerful Serverless data warehouse capable of querying petabytes of data in seconds; Vertex AI provides a complete ML platform; GKE (Google Kubernetes Engine) is the birthplace of Kubernetes with industry-leading container orchestration capabilities. Large internet enterprises including YouTube, Snapchat, and Twitter use GCP's infrastructure. Google's global private network provides extremely low-latency global traffic transmission. For AI/ML-intensive workloads and data analytics scenarios, GCP is one of the technically optimal choices, offering $300 free credits for new users to try.
digitalocean: DigitalOcean is a cloud computing platform designed specifically for developers and SMBs, known for its clean and easy-to-use interface, transparent pricing, and excellent documentation, making it a friendly alternative to AWS's complexity. Droplets VMs start at $4/month, with Managed Kubernetes, Managed Database, and App Platform providing an all-in-one application deployment experience. Rich tutorial documentation is an important learning resource for the tech community, with each in-depth tutorial read by hundreds of thousands of developers. Spaces object storage is fully S3-compatible with extremely low migration costs. Offering $200 free credits for new users with transparent on-demand pricing and no hidden fees, it is the ideal cloud platform for independent developers, startups, and small-to-medium web applications.
cloudflare-workers: Cloudflare Workers is Cloudflare's edge serverless computing platform, allowing developers to deploy code written in JavaScript, Rust, Python, and other languages to Cloudflare's 300+ global data centers, running code near users for extremely low latency. No cold start issues, with each request execution limited to 50ms (CPU time), making it ideal for API proxying, response modification, A/B testing, and middleware scenarios. KV storage, Durable Objects, and R2 object storage build a complete edge application infrastructure. The free tier provides 100,000 requests per day, with paid tiers offering more quota and features. It is one of the optimal choices for building globally low-latency APIs and edge computing applications, deeply integrated with Next.js, Remix, and other frameworks.
hetzner: Hetzner is a veteran German cloud service and dedicated server provider, known for extremely competitive pricing and excellent hardware quality, with an outstanding reputation in the European developer community. Its Cloud VPS prices are 3-5x lower than AWS and DigitalOcean, with industry-leading value for money. Dedicated servers provide powerful computing resources, with bare-metal servers suitable for high-performance computing scenarios. Data centers are located in Nuremberg, Frankfurt, Germany and Helsinki, Finland, compliant with EU GDPR data protection requirements. Hetzner Object Storage provides cheap S3-compatible storage. For European users, developers, and SMBs focused on cost control, Hetzner is the most economical choice for quality cloud infrastructure, particularly suitable for self-hosted application and game server deployment scenarios.
linode: Linode (now Akamai Cloud) is a veteran VPS and cloud computing provider founded in 2003, with significantly improved performance after Akamai acquisition through the global CDN network. Known for stability and reliability, transparent pricing, and quality support, with a consistently high reputation in the developer community. Compute, Storage, Database, Kubernetes, and other services cover complete cloud application needs at 30-50% lower prices than the three major cloud platforms. 11 globally distributed data centers cover Asia-Pacific, Europe, and North America. Free trials provide $100 over 60 days with excellent technical documentation and tutorial quality. It is a reliable choice for developers and enterprises seeking AWS alternatives, with a stable loyal user base particularly in North American and European markets.
vultr: Vultr is a high-performance SSD cloud server provider, widely popular among developers for its extensive coverage with 32 global data centers and flexible billing (hourly billing, starting from $2.5/month). Offers complete cloud services including cloud computing, bare-metal servers, Kubernetes, managed databases, and object storage. Outstanding network performance with 10Gbps uplink bandwidth suitable for traffic-intensive applications. One-click deployment of popular application stacks like WordPress, LAMP, and LEMP with a good getting-started experience. Vultr's global data center coverage includes Asia-Pacific nodes like Tokyo, Seoul, and Singapore, friendly to Asian users. Offering $100 free credits, it is a popular VPS choice for developers focused on performance and global coverage.
render: Render is a modern cloud application hosting platform positioned as Heroku's successor, rapidly gaining developer recognition for its ultra-simple deployment experience and complete service ecosystem. Supports static websites, web services, background workers, Cron jobs, and private services, covering nearly all application deployment scenarios. Managed PostgreSQL and Redis databases are ready to use immediately, with automatic TLS certificates and custom domains requiring no extra configuration. Automatic deployment from GitHub with support for Preview environments generating individual previews for each PR. Offering a generous free tier (static websites permanently free) with reasonable paid plan pricing. Compared to Railway, Render's ecosystem is more mature with better documentation, making it a reliable choice for full-stack application hosting that has rapidly accumulated a large user base among independent developers and startups.
fly: Fly.io is a next-generation container and edge computing-based application deployment platform that lets developers rapidly deploy Docker applications to 35+ global regions, running at the location closest to users for extremely low latency. Its unique Anycast network routes traffic to the nearest healthy instance, different from traditional single-region deployment. Supports persistent storage (Fly Volumes), managed PostgreSQL and Redis, with Fly Machines providing lightweight VMs that start and stop on demand. The Elixir Phoenix and Rails communities particularly favor Fly.io's globally distributed deployment capabilities. Free tier provides certain quotas, with paid billing based on actual usage. It is the ideal platform for developers pursuing global low latency and wanting simple edge deployment implementation, with extremely high goodwill and growth momentum in the tech community.
tailwindcss: Tailwind CSS is currently the most popular utility-first CSS framework, fundamentally changing frontend styling development by providing hundreds of atomic utility classes (like flex, pt-4, text-center) to build designs directly in HTML. Without writing custom CSS, developers compose class names to achieve any design, dramatically improving development speed. JIT (Just-In-Time) compilation mode generates CSS on demand, keeping production bundle sizes extremely small. Tailwind UI provides hundreds of professionally designed component templates, while HeadlessUI provides unstyled accessible components. Works seamlessly with React, Vue, Next.js, and other mainstream frameworks. Completely free and open-source with over 30 million monthly npm downloads, it has become the most mainstream CSS solution in modern frontend development, deeply loved by frontend teams at top companies like Vercel and GitHub.
bootstrap: Bootstrap is the world's most widely used frontend CSS framework, developed by Twitter engineers, providing a responsive grid system, ready-made UI components (buttons, forms, navbars, modals, etc.), and JavaScript plugins to help developers quickly build mobile-first web interfaces. Consistently ranking among GitHub's most popular repositories since 2013, it educated a generation of frontend developers in responsive design thinking. Bootstrap 5 removed jQuery dependencies, using pure CSS variables for enhanced theme customization. The Sass variable system supports deep customization, with large numbers of free and paid theme templates greatly enriching the ecosystem. Completely free and open-source, although partially replaced by Tailwind in modern projects, it remains an irreplaceable efficient choice for rapid prototyping, internal tools, and traditional projects.
vscode: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is Microsoft's free and open-source code editor, currently the world's most popular editor with over 14 million monthly active users. Built on Electron, compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux, supporting syntax highlighting, code completion, and debugging for virtually every programming language. The extension marketplace has over 50,000 plugins covering AI assistance (GitHub Copilot), themes, language support, and virtually every development need. Built-in Git integration, terminal, and debugger provide an excellent out-of-the-box experience. Live Share supports real-time multi-user collaborative programming. Remote Development extensions support seamless development in containers, remote servers, and WSL. It is the preferred editor for most modern development scenarios including web development, Python data science, and cloud-native development.
jetbrains: JetBrains is the benchmark company in professional developer tools, with its IntelliJ IDEA (Java/Kotlin), PyCharm (Python), WebStorm (JavaScript), GoLand (Go), CLion (C++), and other IDEs renowned for deep language understanding and intelligent code assistance, deeply favored by professional developers and enterprise teams. Their code refactoring, error detection, intelligent completion, and database tools far exceed ordinary editors. JetBrains AI Assistant deeply integrates AI programming assistance into IDEs. The All Products Pack subscription supports using all IDE products. Offering monthly and annual subscriptions, with free licenses available for open-source projects and students. It is the preferred tool for professional developers seeking ultimate code writing efficiency, nearly standard configuration in Java and Kotlin ecosystems.
xcode: Xcode is Apple's official integrated development environment for iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS app development, the only official toolchain for developing Apple platform applications. Built-in Swift and Objective-C compilers, Interface Builder visual UI designer, simulator, performance analysis tools (Instruments), and app signing and publishing tools. Swift Playgrounds enables beginners to interactively learn Swift programming. Xcode Cloud provides CI/CD continuous integration services directly integrated with App Store Connect. Completely free but only available on Mac, it is an essential tool every Apple developer must master, while also being the gateway to Apple's development ecosystem — Xcode must be installed to run and publish iOS apps on real devices.
android-studio: Android Studio is Google's official Android app development IDE, built on JetBrains IntelliJ IDEA, providing a complete Android development toolchain including code editor, debugger, performance analysis tools, layout editor, and Android emulator. First-class support for Kotlin and Java combined with intelligent code suggestions dramatically improves development efficiency. Jetpack Compose preview lets developers view UI component effects in real-time. Android Profiler deeply analyzes application CPU, memory, and network usage. Gradle build system manages dependencies and build processes. Completely free and the standard tool for Android app development, Google continuously updates and improves it through I/O conferences each year, making it the core work environment for Android developers.
sublime: Sublime Text is a code and text editor known for extremely fast startup speed and smooth editing experience, the preferred choice for many developers before VS Code became popular. Goto Anything (Ctrl+P) enables instant jumping between any file, symbol, and code line; multi-cursor editing and multi-selection make batch operations extremely efficient; Command Palette centralizes all feature commands. Package Control package manager provides extensive plugin extensions. Its ability to handle large files far surpasses VS Code, remaining fluid even with GB-sized files. Uses a one-time purchase license model with unlimited free trial (with occasional purchase prompts), providing paid plans with 3 years of license updates. Still has a considerable loyal user base among developers with extreme performance requirements and text processing professionals.
vim: Vim is the most influential command-line text editor in Unix tradition, renowned for modal editing (Normal, Insert, Visual modes) and keyboard-driven ultimate efficiency, where developers who master Vim can edit efficiently without ever touching a mouse. Enduring for 50+ years, it has become the pre-installed editor on virtually all Unix/Linux systems, an essential skill for remote server development. Neovim is a modernized Vim fork with Lua configuration support and native LSP integration, rapidly becoming the preferred choice for the next generation of Vim users. Despite a steep learning curve, once mastered, the editing efficiency and keyboard muscle memory benefit developers for a lifetime. Completely free and open-source with one of the most loyal developer communities.
emacs: GNU Emacs is the longest-standing and most powerful extensible text editor, known for the Emacs Lisp configuration language and the philosophy of living inside the editor. Through Lisp plugins, Emacs can be extended into an email client, file manager, terminal, even a web browser — a truly all-purpose tool. Org Mode is one of Emacs's most admired features, providing powerful plain-text task management and writing environments deeply loved by scholars and writers. Doom Emacs and Spacemacs are popular pre-configured distributions that lower the barrier to entry. Like Vim, Emacs has an extremely loyal core user base, offering a highly personalized customized editing experience once mastered. Completely free and open-source, representing a unique development philosophy and cultural tradition.
notepadpp: Notepad++ is the most popular free text editor on Windows, known for being lightweight and fast, practically useful, and completely free, consistently the preferred replacement for Windows' native Notepad. Supports syntax highlighting for over 80 programming languages, multi-tab editing of multiple files simultaneously, powerful find and replace (including regular expressions), as well as macro recording and code folding. Plugin manager provides many extensions, with FTP plugin supporting direct editing of remote files. Completely free and open-source under the GNU GPL license with no ads and no paid feature restrictions. Although less feature-rich than VS Code, its fast startup, low resource usage, and simple direct user experience make it irreplaceable for quickly viewing and editing text files, particularly suitable for everyday lightweight editing needs of Windows users.
bing: Bing is Microsoft's search engine and the world's second largest, experiencing a strong resurgence in recent years through deep integration of AI capabilities. Bing Chat (now Microsoft Copilot) combines GPT-4 level AI conversation capabilities with real-time web search, allowing users to conduct AI conversations directly in the search box and receive answers with cited sources. Image search quality is industry-leading, with an excellent video search experience. Bing's rewards points program (Microsoft Rewards) lets users accumulate points through searching to redeem gift cards. As Windows' default search engine, it has a stable user base. For users comfortable with the Microsoft ecosystem or wanting to combine AI search with traditional search, Bing provides a high-quality search experience that differs from Google.
duckduckgo: DuckDuckGo is the search engine most trusted by privacy-conscious users globally, with a core promise of not tracking user search history, not building user profiles, and not displaying ads based on personal information. With over 100 million daily searches, it is one of the most important privacy alternatives to Google. The Bangs feature (entering !g to search Google directly, !w for Wikipedia) dramatically improves search efficiency. DuckDuckGo Browser provides Android and iOS versions with built-in tracker blocking and forced HTTPS, with Email Protection filtering email trackers. Completely free and profitable through non-personalized advertising, proving the viability of a privacy-respecting business model, it is the preferred search engine for privacy-conscious users replacing Google.
wolframalpha: Wolfram Alpha is a computational knowledge engine different from traditional search engines, capable of directly computing and answering factual questions in mathematics, science, engineering, history, geography, and other fields rather than returning webpage links. Enter a math formula to receive solving steps, enter a compound name to get molecular structure and properties, enter two city names to get distance and timezone comparisons. Particularly powerful in math education, it can show detailed solving steps for calculus, linear algebra, and statistics. Founded by mathematician Stephen Wolfram and built on the Mathematica computing engine. Offering free basic queries and Wolfram Alpha Pro paid tier (complete solution steps, more data, and API access), it is a powerful computational assistance tool for students, engineers, researchers, and data scientists.
wikipedia: Wikipedia is the world's largest free multilingual online encyclopedia, written and maintained by millions of volunteers from around the world, covering over 62 million articles in 300+ languages. An open collaborative model and continuous community review ensure content quality, making it an important starting point for knowledge queries for scholars, researchers, and ordinary users. Although Wikipedia should not be directly cited as an academic source, its rich reference lists are valuable leads for deeper research. The Wikimedia Foundation operates Wikipedia and its sister projects through donations. Wikimedia Commons provides millions of freely licensed images and media files. Wikipedia's mission is to provide free knowledge to all of humanity, making it one of the most important public knowledge assets on the internet.
medium: Medium is a high-quality content creation and reading platform founded by Twitter co-founder Ev Williams, aggregating in-depth articles in technology, startups, design, writing, psychology, and other fields. The platform's unique reading experience is extremely clean and elegant, with authors receiving revenue shares based on actual reading time, incentivizing high-quality long-form content creation. The Medium Partner Program enables quality authors to earn substantial monthly writing income. Readers access all paid-wall content through monthly memberships ($5/month). Daily curated recommendations help discover high-quality content. It is an important platform for tech professionals, entrepreneurs, product managers, and thought leaders to share deep insights, and one of the best reading destinations for high-quality English long-form content.
pocket: Pocket is Mozilla's read-later app that allows users to save interesting articles, videos, and web pages for offline reading at any time, an effective tool against information fragmentation and impulse immediate consumption. Browser extensions and mobile one-click saving automatically parse content into clean, ad-free reading format. Tag management and full-text search help organize and retrieve saved content. Pocket Recommended personalized recommendations are high quality. Offline reading is extremely practical for commuting and travel scenarios. Offering a free tier (with ads) and Pocket Premium paid tier (permanent storage, highlights, and no ads), it is a lightweight and convenient tool for heavy content consumers and researchers to manage their reading lists.
instapaper: Instapaper is a classic read-later service known for minimalist design and excellent reading experience, now independently operated. The core feature saves any webpage in one click as a clean plain-text reading format, removing ads and distracting elements to focus on the text itself. Supports reading interface customization including font size, line spacing, and background color, with light/dark mode switching. Offline reading support and Kindle sending features are favorites of heavy readers. Text highlighting and notes features help mark important content with notes exportable to Evernote and other tools. Offering limited functionality in the free tier and a Premium paid tier unlocking all features, it is the preferred read-later tool for users seeking a simple and pure reading experience.
readwise: Readwise is a reading tool designed for knowledge digestion and memory retention, with its core feature aggregating user highlights from Kindle, Instapaper, Pocket, and Apple Books into one place, using Spaced Repetition algorithms to push daily reviews, helping truly absorb and internalize what has been read. Deep integration with Notion, Obsidian, Roam Research, Logseq, and other note-taking tools automatically syncs highlights to personal knowledge bases. Readwise Reader is a newly launched all-in-one reading app supporting RSS subscriptions, newsletters, and Twitter lists for unified management of all reading content. Offering monthly and annual subscription plans, it is an indispensable tool for learners who take knowledge management and reading notes seriously, highly popular among knowledge workers and learning communities.
omnivore: Omnivore is a completely free and open-source read-later application providing web article saving and reading features similar to Readwise and Instapaper, but completely free with open-source code allowing self-hosting. Supports unified collection and management of articles, newsletter subscriptions, PDFs, and Twitter threads, with flexible tag and filter organization. Full-text search is powerful, with highlights and annotations exportable to Obsidian, Notion, and Logseq knowledge base tools. Mobile apps support iOS and Android with complete offline reading features. For users who value data sovereignty and are unwilling to pay for read-later features, Omnivore is the most feature-complete free alternative, with an excellent reputation among independent developers and privacy-conscious user communities.
google-workspace: Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) is Google's cloud office collaboration suite for enterprises and teams, integrating core productivity tools including Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, and Calendar. All applications are cloud-based supporting real-time multi-user collaborative editing without local installation, seamlessly accessible across devices. Business Gmail provides custom domain email, while Meet supports HD video conferencing. AI assistant Duet AI is deeply integrated across products, providing smart writing, auto-summary, and meeting notes features. Offering Business Starter, Standard, Plus, and Enterprise subscription tiers with over 10 million enterprise users globally. For teams prioritizing collaboration efficiency and preferring the Google ecosystem, it is one of the most fluid cloud office solutions available.
microsoft-365: Microsoft 365 (formerly Office 365) is Microsoft's enterprise and personal cloud office subscription service, including the complete Office suite of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, and more, replacing traditional one-time purchases with subscriptions to ensure continuous access to the latest feature updates. Teams has become the core platform for enterprise video conferencing and collaboration, deeply integrated with the entire Office suite. The Copilot AI assistant provides smart writing, data analysis, and auto-summary features across Office applications. Family plans allow multiple people to share subscriptions, while business plans provide enterprise-grade security and management features. For users and enterprises that have long used the Office suite, Microsoft 365 is the most feature-complete and compatible cloud office choice.
dropbox: Dropbox is the pioneer of cloud storage, being the first to bring the file synchronization concept to the masses, now with over 700 million registered users. Seamlessly syncs local folders with the cloud, supporting real-time access to all files across devices, with version history enabling recovery to any point in time. Dropbox Paper provides lightweight collaborative document functionality, while Dropbox Sign (formerly HelloSign) supports electronic signatures. Smart Sync syncs only file metadata locally to save disk space with on-demand downloads. Team editions provide admin consoles, team folders, and permission management. Offering 2GB free storage and Plus, Professional, Business paid plans, it is a reliable tool for personal file backup and cross-device sync, also widely used for enterprise document sharing and collaboration.
box: Box is a cloud storage platform focused on enterprise content management and secure file sharing, known for powerful security and compliance capabilities, widely adopted by Fortune 500 companies in finance, healthcare, and legal industries. Provides AES-256 encryption, granular permission controls, detailed access logs, and compliance reports meeting strict regulatory requirements like HIPAA and FedRAMP. Box Sign supports electronic signatures, while Box Skills provides AI content analysis and metadata extraction. Deep integration with 1,500+ applications including Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, and Slack. Offering a personal free tier and Business, Business Plus, Enterprise paid plans for enterprises, it is the preferred cloud content management platform for enterprises with extreme data security and compliance requirements.
onedrive: OneDrive is Microsoft's cloud storage and file synchronization service, deeply integrated with Windows 11, Microsoft 365, and Office applications, making it the most convenient cloud storage choice for users in the Microsoft ecosystem. Windows users have it out of the box, automatically backing up desktop, documents, and pictures folders with seamless cross-device sync. Office files in OneDrive support real-time multi-user collaborative editing with save-to-sync functionality. Personal Vault provides an extra security layer for storing sensitive files. Microsoft 365 subscribers automatically receive 1TB of storage, with personal editions offering 5GB free storage. Deeply embedded in the Windows and Office ecosystems, it is the natural choice for Microsoft users for file backup, cross-device access, and team file sharing.
google-drive: Google Drive is Google's cloud storage service, giving every Google account user 15GB of free storage usable across Gmail, Google Photos, and Drive. Seamlessly integrated with productivity tools including Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Forms, supporting real-time multi-user collaborative document editing with an industry-leading collaboration experience. Supports storage for virtually any file format, with powerful search that can recognize file content, image text, and even text in scanned PDFs. Google One paid subscriptions provide expanded storage from 100GB to 2TB. Mobile apps are fully featured with offline access supporting continued file editing without internet. For Android users and Google service users, Google Drive is the most natural cloud storage and file collaboration hub.
icloud: iCloud is Apple's cloud service platform, deeply embedded in the operating systems and native apps of iPhone, iPad, and Mac, providing photo sync, file storage, contact and calendar backup, iCloud Mail, and other services. iCloud Photos automatically syncs photos and videos across all Apple devices, while iCloud Drive stores documents and files syncing between devices. Family Sharing allows up to 6 family members to share subscriptions. Every Apple ID user receives 5GB of free storage, with iCloud+ paid plans providing 50GB to 2TB of storage plus additional privacy protection features including Hide My Email and iCloud Private Relay. For Apple ecosystem users, iCloud is the most convenient solution for keeping multiple devices in sync and safely backing up data.
wetransfer: WeTransfer is one of the most popular large file transfer services, with free users able to transfer up to 2GB of files in a single transfer without registering an account — just enter the recipient's email and send, with links valid for 7 days. The interface is extremely simple: drag and drop files, enter email addresses, and sharing is complete within seconds. WeTransfer Pro provides 200GB transfer quota, custom branded pages, link password protection, and permanent storage. The Collect feature allows creating inspiration and material collection boards. Widely used in the global creative industry, particularly favored by designers, photographers, and video production companies, it is a convenient tool for quickly delivering large design files and materials to clients without needing complex cloud storage services.
notion-ai: Notion AI is an artificial intelligence writing and productivity assistant deeply built into the Notion workspace, enabling users to complete content generation, editing, translation, and summarization tasks with AI without leaving Notion, integrating AI capabilities into daily workflows. Writing assistance can continue articles, improve writing style, correct grammar, and adjust tone; summarization extracts core points from long documents in one click; translation supports multiple languages. AI can directly manipulate Notion databases, generating content to fill tables based on conditions. For heavy Notion users, Notion AI is the most natural way to improve content production efficiency within a familiar work environment. Billed monthly as an add-on to Notion subscriptions, it significantly reduces the friction cost of using AI in workflows.
chatpdf: ChatPDF is an AI-based PDF document conversation tool that allows users to upload any PDF file and ask questions directly in natural language, with AI extracting relevant information from the document and providing precise answers without reading the entire document. Suitable for quickly understanding the core content of academic papers, legal contracts, financial reports, technical manuals, and other long documents. Supports multi-language questioning and answering — even if the document is in English, questions can be asked in Chinese to receive Chinese answers. Citation features mark the original text paragraphs corresponding to answers, enhancing credibility. Offering daily free upload quotas and a Plus paid tier (unlimited uploads, larger files, and more conversations), it is a practical tool for students, researchers, legal professionals, and business people to efficiently process large volumes of document information.
asana: Asana is a project and task management platform trusted by teams worldwide, helping teams coordinate work, clarify responsibilities, and track progress, efficiently managing everything from daily tasks to complex projects. Supports multiple views including lists, kanban, timeline (Gantt chart), and workload to meet different project management needs. Workflow automation triggers notifications, assigns tasks, and updates status to reduce manual operations. Seamlessly integrates with 300+ tools including Slack, Google Drive, Microsoft 365, Zoom, and Salesforce. The Goals feature connects daily tasks to company strategic objectives to enhance the sense of work meaning. Offering a free tier (up to 15 people) and Premium, Business, Enterprise paid plans, adopted by companies like NASA, Spotify, and Airbnb, it is a reliable choice for medium to large team project management.
monday: Monday.com is a flexible Work OS used by over 200,000 organizations, renowned for its highly visual colorful interface and powerful customization capabilities. Users can build customized workflows tailored to specific team needs, supporting business scenarios including task management, CRM, project planning, and marketing calendars. Automation features are powerful with complex cross-platform trigger rules configurable. Monday Dev focuses on software development workflows, while Monday Sales CRM covers sales management scenarios. Deep integration with Slack, Google Workspace, Jira, Salesforce, and other tools. Offering a personal free tier and Basic, Standard, Pro, Enterprise paid plans, it continues rapid growth in the project management tool market with outstanding user experience and flexibility.
basecamp: Basecamp is a project collaboration tool known for its minimalist philosophy, developed by 37signals and adhering to an all-in-one concept that integrates messages, tasks, files, calendars, discussions, and check-ins in an extremely simple interface. The unique client project mode allows external clients to safely participate in project collaboration without seeing internal discussions. Hill Charts progress visualization vividly shows the uphill and downhill phases of tasks. Unlike other tools, Basecamp uses simple flat pricing — a fixed monthly fee for unlimited projects and unlimited users without per-seat billing, offering excellent value for large teams. It is the ideal choice for teams prioritizing clean workflows and resisting tool overload, with significant influence in advocating remote work culture.
confluence: Confluence is Atlassian's enterprise-grade team knowledge base and document collaboration platform, deeply integrated with Jira to form the core information hub for software development teams. Supports hierarchical knowledge management with pages, blogs, templates, and Spaces, where teams document technical documentation, product specifications, meeting notes, and internal processes. Powerful search quickly locates any historical document, with page comments and inline comments supporting precise discussions. Deep integration with Jira, Trello, Slack, GitHub, and other tools makes it the standard knowledge management tool for tech companies with strong engineering culture. Offering a free tier (up to 10 people) and paid tiers, it is important infrastructure for building team knowledge assets and documentation systems.
jira: Jira is the world's largest market share software development project management tool by Atlassian, used by software teams at over 65,000 enterprises globally. Designed specifically for agile development supporting both Scrum and Kanban workflows, with complete Sprint planning, Backlog management, and burndown chart features. Custom workflows support complex Issue status transitions, with automation rules reducing manual operations. Deep integration with Confluence, Bitbucket, GitHub, Slack, and other tools builds a complete software development lifecycle management system. Offering a free tier (up to 10 people) and Standard, Premium, Enterprise paid plans, it is the core tool for medium to large software development teams for requirement management, bug tracking, and agile iteration.
evernote: Evernote is a pioneer in the established note-taking app space, renowned for cross-platform sync, powerful search, and flexible note organization, supporting text, images, voice, web clipping, PDFs, and other content types. The web clipper browser extension saves any web page content in one click, with smart search even recognizing text in images and handwritten notes. Tags, notebooks, and shortcuts build a flexible personal knowledge base system. Integrates with Google Drive, Slack, Outlook, and other tools. Offering a free basic tier and Personal, Professional, Teams paid subscriptions, it still has tens of millions of loyal users after years of development, suitable for long-term users accustomed to its workflow, particularly outstanding for web content collection and organization.
todoist: Todoist is one of the best-designed cross-platform task management apps, renowned for its elegant minimalist interface and powerful natural language input, supporting seamless sync across iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, browsers, and all other platforms. Natural language recognition automatically parses phrases like meeting tomorrow at 3pm into tasks with reminders, making task addition extremely efficient. Priority levels, labels, filters, and project views help organize and focus on the most important work. The Karma points system uses gamification mechanisms to encourage users to maintain productivity habits. Offering a feature-complete free tier and Pro and Business paid tiers, named Best App by Time magazine, it is an elegant solution for personal task management and small team collaboration.
forest: Forest is a focus management app combining the Pomodoro Technique with a tree-planting game, where users cannot leave the app while a tree-growing timer runs, earning a virtual tree upon completion and building a green forest, while leaving early causes the tree to wither — visually cultivating focus habits. Forest partners with real charitable organizations, where virtual credits accumulated by users can be redeemed to plant real trees in Africa, converting digital focus into environmental action. Supports white noise background sounds, friend group planting, and statistics reports. Available as a paid download for iOS and Android plus a free Chrome extension, it is deeply loved by students, writers, and anyone wanting to reduce phone dependency, with massive five-star reviews accumulated on the App Store.
rescuetime: RescueTime is an automatic time tracking and productivity analysis tool that runs silently in the background, automatically recording time spent on every app, website, and file to generate detailed productivity reports without manual timekeeping. Smart categorization divides activities into productive, neutral, and distracting tiers to help users objectively understand their time allocation. Focus sessions can block distracting websites, with daily goal settings helping establish healthy work habits. Detailed weekly reports and trend analysis let users track productivity changes long-term. Offering a basic free tier and RescueTime Premium paid tier, it is an important tool for knowledge workers, freelancers, and professionals who want to improve time management to deeply understand their own work patterns.
fantastical: Fantastical is widely recognized as the best calendar app on Mac and iOS platforms, earning a large loyal following with powerful natural language event creation, elegant interface design, and a complete feature set. Entering meet with John tomorrow at 10am for 1 hour automatically recognizes and creates a calendar event with invitations, with extremely high operation efficiency. Supports multi-account management for iCloud, Google Calendar, Office 365, and Exchange, with smooth DayTicker week view and month view switching. Task management integrates with Reminders, while Fantastical for Teams supports team calendar sharing. Offering 14-day free trials and annual subscriptions, it is a high-quality productivity tool that heavy Apple ecosystem users are willing to pay for, having received multiple Apple App of the Year nominations.
google-analytics: Google Analytics (GA4) is the world's most widely used website and app data analytics platform, helping website owners and marketers deeply understand user behavior, traffic sources, and conversion paths. GA4 uses an event-based data model providing full-journey user tracking with more precise cross-device attribution analysis. Real-time reports, audience analysis, funnel visualization, and custom dashboards make data insights readily accessible. Deep integration with Google Ads, Search Console, and BigQuery forms a complete digital marketing data ecosystem. Completely free for websites with under 100,000 monthly visits, with Analytics 360 enterprise edition providing higher data quotas and SLA guarantees for large enterprises.
